title: Ful Medames with Cumin, Lemon and Tomato
summary: Canned fava beans simmered in garlic and cumin oil, half-mashed into a thick stew, brightened with lemon and topped with tomato, onion and parsley.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon juice, plus lemon wedges to serve

steps.title: Bloom garlic and cumin
steps.text: Put the 3 tbsp oil, garlic and cumin in the saucepan over medium heat and warm for about 2 min. Pull it from the heat if the garlic starts to colour; you want it fragrant, not brown, which would turn it bitter.

steps.title: Simmer the beans
steps.text: Add the beans, 300 ml water, salt and pepper and simmer for 8-10 min, stirring now and then. The liquid will thicken slightly as the beans soften and release starch.

steps.title: Mash half
steps.text: Off the heat, roughly mash about half the beans with the masher and leave the rest whole for texture. The result should look like a thick, spoonable stew. Stir in the lemon juice and taste.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Spoon into a shallow bowl and scatter over the tomato, onion and parsley. Finish with a generous swirl of olive oil and serve with lemon wedges.

tips: Over-mashing into a smooth purée is a common mistake; keep plenty of whole beans.
Canned beans vary in saltiness, so taste before adding more salt.
Add lemon off the heat to keep its flavour fresh.
Warm pita and sliced cucumber are traditional on the side.
storage: Refrigerate the beans (without toppings) covered up to 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C), then add fresh toppings. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
